title: Refurbished Laptop Grades Explained: Grade A vs B vs C
content:
When you shop for a refurbished laptop you will see labels like Grade A, A+, B or C. These refurbished laptop grades describe how the laptop looks, not how it performs. There is no single official standard, so each seller defines them a little differently. This guide explains the common meanings so you can compare like with like.

The common grading scale

Grade is about looks, not performance

A properly refurbished Grade B laptop should work exactly like a Grade A one. The processor, RAM, SSD, ports and battery are what decide performance, so always check those specs alongside the grade. A Grade A laptop with a worn-out battery can be a worse buy than a Grade B unit with a healthy one.

What to ask when a seller lists a grade

  • Can I see real photos of this exact unit, not stock photos?
  • Are there any screen marks or dead pixels?
  • What is the battery health or cycle count?
  • Has anything been replaced, such as the keyboard, screen or battery?
  • Does the warranty differ between grades?

Frequently asked questions

What does Grade A refurbished mean?

Grade A usually means the laptop shows only light signs of use, with a clean screen and keyboard. Definitions vary by seller, so ask for photos of the exact unit.

Is a Grade B refurbished laptop worth buying?

Yes, if you don't mind visible scratches. A properly refurbished Grade B laptop performs the same as Grade A and usually costs less.

Does the grade affect performance?

No. Grades describe cosmetic condition. Performance depends on the processor, RAM, storage and battery health.

Is there an official refurbished grading standard?

There is no single official standard used by all sellers, so compare descriptions and photos rather than relying on the grade label alone.
